messages:
Elaine: Heads-up — Acme POC kicks off tomorrow. They asked for a dedicated endpoint and strict IP allowlisting on their side. Can we confirm the egress IPs they should expect from our dedicated pool?
Chris SE: Quick clarifier — they want to allow inbound to our dedicated endpoint or expect our egress to be static so their downstream webhooks can reach customer endpoints?
Elaine: They will call our dedicated endpoint from their app, so they need our endpoint's IP in their allowlist. Also they asked if we can block outbound egress from the inference instances to external internet (no callbacks).
Nina (Infra): We just provisioned a dedicated pool in us-east-1 for this POC. For dedicated endpoints we can provide static NAT egress IPs. Current NAT IPs for that pool: 34.201.100.12, 34.201.100.13.
Sam (SRE): Note — those NAT IPs are shared within the dedicated pool unless we carve a private VPC path. If Acme needs exclusive egress IPs we can provision a reserved NAT or route via their VPC (Private mode). That takes ~1 business day.
Laura (Security): Blocking outbound egress from inference is doable via egress rules on the host and firewall. We need to understand which external domains (if any) must remain reachable — model downloads are already pre-cached on the dedicated pool.
Elaine: They want no outbound external calls during the POC. Also they requested a short-lived API key to avoid sharing a long-lived credential in an email. Any recommended pattern?
Chris SE: We'll issue a temporary API key tied to the POC org with a TTL of 48h and rate limit 10rps. Use header: Authorization: Bearer redwood-temp-POC-abc123. Example curl (safe to paste in support ticket):
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer redwood-temp-POC-abc123' https://dedicated-acme-us-east.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}'
```
Elaine: Perfect. Can we also share the endpoint DNS name for their firewall team so they can do an allowlist by FQDN as backup?
Nina (Infra): DNS for the endpoint: dedicated-acme-us-east.redwood.ai. If they prefer IP allowlist we gave the two NAT IPs above. FQDN resolves to those IPs behind the load balancer.
deploy-bot: provision complete — dedicated-endpoint dedicated-acme-us-east created at 2026-03-19T23:33:10Z.
Sam (SRE): Small gotcha: if we need to rotate the NAT or scale the pool, IPs can change unless we reserve them. For the POC we'll reserve the two NAT addresses for the week. If Acme needs absolute SLA on static egress for longer, we recommend Dedicated + Private wiring.
Laura (Security): For the security questionnaire: addendum — POC temporary key will be scoped to read/write for the specific model endpoint and will be logged. We can redact logs on request. Also we can provide the SOC docs link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc (send via secure channel).
Elaine: Action items — (1) send Acme temporary key and endpoint DNS (2) confirm their firewall has the two NAT IPs (34.201.100.12/13) and FQDN (3) set egress to deny-all on the dedicated pool for the POC. I'll draft the message to their infra lead.
Chris SE: Pricing note for sales — short POC (<=2 weeks) on Dedicated pool: bill at trial rate, estimate ~ $X/day depending on throughput. I'll DM you details.
Elaine: Thanks all — sending now. If anything flips I'll start a new thread. :thumbsup:
